6	module
7	
8	public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Presheaf.Generator
9	public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Presheaf.Pushforward
10	public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.PartialAdjoint
11	public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.CompositionIso
12	
13	/-!
14	# Pullback of presheaves of modules
15	
16	Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a functor, `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` and `S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` be presheaves
17	of rings, and `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R` be a morphism of presheaves of rings,
18	we introduce the pullback functor `pullback : PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R`
19	as the left adjoint of `pushforward : PresheafOfModules R ⥤ PresheafOfModules S`.
20	The existence of this left adjoint functor is obtained under suitable universe assumptions.
21	
22	From the compatibility of `pushforward` with respect to composition, we deduce
23	similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.
24	
25	-/
26	
27	@[expose] public section
28	
29	universe v v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄ u₁ u₂ u₃ u₄ u
30	
31	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite Functor
32	
33	namespace PresheafOfModules
34	
35	section
36	
37	variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
38	  {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
39	  [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
40	
41	/-- The pullback functor `PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R` induced by
42	a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, defined as the left adjoint
43	functor to the pushforward, when it exists. -/
44	noncomputable def pullback : PresheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R :=
45	  (pushforward.{v} φ).leftAdjoint
46	
47	/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, this is the adjunction
48	between associated pullback and pushforward functors on the categories
49	of presheaves of modules. -/
50	noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction : pullback.{v} φ ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
51	  Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (pushforward φ)
52	
53	/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, this is the property
54	that the (partial) left adjoint functor of `pushforward φ` is defined
55	on a certain object `M : PresheafOfModules S`. -/
56	abbrev pullbackObjIsDefined : ObjectProperty (PresheafOfModules.{v} S) :=
57	  (pushforward φ).leftAdjointObjIsDefined
58	
59	end
60	
61	section
62	
63	variable {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
64	  {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
65	
66	/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, where `F : C ⥤ D`,
67	`S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat`, `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` and `X : C`, the (partial) left adjoint
68	functor of `pushforward φ` is defined on the object `(free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)`:
69	this object shall be mapped to `(free R).obj (yoneda.obj (F.obj X))`. -/
70	noncomputable def pushforwardCompCoyonedaFreeYonedaCorepresentableBy (X : C) :
71	    (pushforward φ ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op ((free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)))).CorepresentableBy
72	      ((free R).obj (yoneda.obj (F.obj X))) where
73	  homEquiv {M} := freeYonedaEquiv.trans
74	    (freeYonedaEquiv (M := (pushforward φ).obj M)).symm
75	  homEquiv_comp {M N} g f := freeYonedaEquiv.injective (by
76	    dsimp
77	    erw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply, freeYonedaEquiv_comp]
78	    conv_rhs => erw [freeYonedaEquiv_comp]
79	    erw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
80	    rfl)
81	
82	lemma pullbackObjIsDefined_free_yoneda (X : C) :
83	    pullbackObjIsDefined φ ((free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)) :=
84	  (pushforwardCompCoyonedaFreeYonedaCorepresentableBy φ X).isCorepresentable
85	
86	lemma pullbackObjIsDefined_eq_top :
87	    pullbackObjIsDefined.{u} φ = ⊤ := by
88	  ext M
89	  simp only [Pi.top_apply, Prop.top_eq_true, iff_true]
90	  apply leftAdjointObjIsDefined_of_isColimit
91	    M.isColimitFreeYonedaCoproductsCokernelCofork
92	  rintro (_ | _)
93	  all_goals
94	    apply leftAdjointObjIsDefined_colimit _
95	      (fun _ ↦ pullbackObjIsDefined_free_yoneda _ _)
96	
97	instance : (pushforward.{u} φ).IsRightAdjoint :=
98	  isRightAdjoint_of_leftAdjointObjIsDefined_eq_top
99	    (pullbackObjIsDefined_eq_top φ)
100	
101	end
102	
103	section
104	
105	variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
106	  {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} E] {E' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} E']
107	
108	variable {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
109	  {G : D ⥤ E} {T : Eᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (ψ : R ⟶ G.op ⋙ T)
110	
111	instance : (pushforward.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S)).IsRightAdjoint :=
112	  isRightAdjoint_of_iso (pushforwardId.{v} S).symm
113	
114	variable (S) in
115	/-- The pullback by the identity morphism identifies to the identity functor of the
116	category of presheaves of modules. -/
117	noncomputable def pullbackId : pullback.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S) ≅ 𝟭 _ :=
118	  ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S))).leftAdjointIdIso (pushforwardId S)
119	
120	variable [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
121	
122	section
123	
124	variable [(pushforward.{v} ψ).IsRightAdjoint]
125	
126	instance : (pushforward.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ)).IsRightAdjoint :=
127	  isRightAdjoint_of_iso (pushforwardComp.{v} φ ψ)
128	
129	/-- The composition of two pullback functors on presheaves of modules identifies
130	to the pullback for the composition. -/
131	noncomputable def pullbackComp :
132	    pullback.{v} φ ⋙ pullback.{v} ψ ≅
133	      pullback.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ) :=
134	  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso
135	    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} φ) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} ψ)
136	    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ))
137	    (pushforwardComp φ ψ)
138	
139	variable {T' : E'ᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {G' : E ⥤ E'} (ψ' : T ⟶ G'.op ⋙ T')
140	  [(pushforward.{v} ψ').IsRightAdjoint]
141	
142	lemma pullback_assoc :
143	    isoWhiskerLeft _ (pullbackComp.{v} ψ ψ') ≪≫
144	      pullbackComp.{v} (G := G ⋙ G') φ (ψ ≫ whiskerLeft G.op ψ') =
145	    (associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫ isoWhiskerRight (pullbackComp.{v} φ ψ) _ ≪≫
146	        pullbackComp.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ) ψ' :=
147	  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_assoc _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (pushforward_assoc φ ψ ψ')
148	
149	end
150	
151	lemma pullback_id_comp :
152	    pullbackComp.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S) φ =
153	      isoWhiskerRight (pullbackId S) (pullback φ) ≪≫ Functor.leftUnitor _ :=
154	  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_id_comp _ _ _ _ (pushforward_comp_id φ)
155	
156	lemma pullback_comp_id :
157	    pullbackComp.{v} (G := 𝟭 _) φ (𝟙 R) =
158	      isoWhiskerLeft _ (pullbackId R) ≪≫ Functor.rightUnitor _ :=
159	  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_comp_id _ _ _ _ (pushforward_id_comp φ)
160	
161	end
162	
163	end PresheafOfModules

13	# Pullback of sheaves of modules
14	
15	Let `S` and `R` be sheaves of rings over sites `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` respectively.
16	Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor between these sites, and
17	let `φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R` be a morphism
18	of sheaves of rings.
19	
20	In this file, we define the pullback functor for sheaves of modules
21	`pullback.{v} φ : SheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} R`
22	that is left adjoint to `pushforward.{v} φ`. We show that it exists
23	under suitable assumptions, and prove that the pullback of (pre)sheaves of
24	modules commutes with the sheafification.
25	
26	From the compatibility of `pushforward` with respect to composition, we deduce
27	similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.
28	
29	-/

31	@[expose] public section
32	
33	universe v v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄ u₁ u₂ u₃ u₄ u
34	
35	open CategoryTheory Functor

40	  {D' : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} D'] {D'' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} D'']
41	  {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {F : C ⥤ D}
42	  {S : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} {R : Sheaf K RingCat.{u}}
43	  [Functor.IsContinuous F J K]
44	  (φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R)

51	a morphism of sheaves of rings `S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R`,
52	defined as the left adjoint functor to the pushforward, when it exists. -/
53	noncomputable def pullback : SheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} R :=
54	  (pushforward.{v} φ).leftAdjoint

57	`S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R`, this is the adjunction
58	between the corresponding pullback and pushforward functors on the categories
59	of sheaves of modules. -/
60	noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction : pullback.{v} φ ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
61	  Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (pushforward φ)
62	
63	instance : (pullback.{v} φ).IsLeftAdjoint :=
64	  (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ).isLeftAdjoint
65	
66	end

68	section

70	variable [(PresheafOfModules.pushforward.{v} φ.hom).IsRightAdjoint]
71	  [HasWeakSheafify K AddCommGrpCat.{v}] [K.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
72

76	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
77	/-- Construction of a left adjoint to the functor `pushforward.{v} φ` by using the
78	pullback of presheaves of modules and the sheafification. -/
79	noncomputable def adjunction :
80	    (forget S ⋙ PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ.hom ⋙
81	      PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj)) ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
82	  Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv
83	    { homEquiv := fun F G ↦
84	        ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 R.obj)).homEquiv _ _).trans
85	            (((PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ.hom).homEquiv F.val G.val).trans
86	              ((fullyFaithfulForget S).homEquiv (Y := (pushforward φ).obj G)).symm)
87	      homEquiv_naturality_left_symm := by
88	        intros
89	        dsimp [Functor.FullyFaithful.homEquiv]
90	        -- these erw seem difficult to remove
91	        erw [Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm,
92	          Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm]
93	        dsimp [pushforward_obj_val]
94	        simp only [Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc]
95	      homEquiv_naturality_right := by
96	        tauto }
97	
98	end PullbackConstruction
99	
100	instance : (pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint :=
101	  (PullbackConstruction.adjunction.{v} φ).isRightAdjoint
102	
103	/-- The pullback functor on sheaves of modules can be described as a composition
104	of the forget functor to presheaves, the pullback on presheaves of modules, and
105	the sheafification functor. -/
106	noncomputable def pullbackIso :
107	    pullback.{v} φ ≅
108	      forget S ⋙ PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ.hom ⋙
109	        PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj) :=
110	  Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ)
111	    (PullbackConstruction.adjunction φ)
112	
113	section
114	
115	variable [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{v}] [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
116	
117	/-- The pullback of (pre)sheaves of modules commutes with the sheafification. -/
118	noncomputable def sheafificationCompPullback :
119	    PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 S.obj) ⋙ pullback.{v} φ ≅
120	      PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ.hom ⋙
121	        PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj) :=
122	  Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq
123	    ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 S.obj)).comp
124	      (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ))
125	    ((PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ.hom).comp
126	      (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 R.obj)))
127	
128	end
129	
130	end
131	
132	
133	instance : (pushforward.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S)).IsRightAdjoint :=
134	  Functor.isRightAdjoint_of_iso (pushforwardId S).symm
135	
136	variable (S) in
137	/-- The pullback by the identity morphism identifies to the identity functor of the
138	category of sheaves of modules. -/
139	noncomputable def pullbackId : pullback.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S) ≅ 𝟭 _ :=
140	  ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S))).leftAdjointIdIso (pushforwardId S)
141	
142	variable (S) in
143	@[simp]
144	lemma conjugateEquiv_pullbackId_hom :
145	    conjugateEquiv .id (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} _) (pullbackId S).hom =
146	      (pushforwardId S).inv :=
147	  Adjunction.conjugateEquiv_leftAdjointIdIso_hom _ _
148	
149	variable [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
150	
151	section
152	
153	variable {K' : GrothendieckTopology D'} {K'' : GrothendieckTopology D''}
154	  {G : D ⥤ D'} {R' : Sheaf K' RingCat.{u}}
155	  [Functor.IsContinuous G K K']
156	  [Functor.IsContinuous (F ⋙ G) J K']
157	  (ψ : R ⟶ (G.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} K K').obj R')
158	
159	variable [(pushforward.{v} ψ).IsRightAdjoint]
160	
161	instance : (pushforward.{v} (F := F ⋙ G)
162	    (φ ≫ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).map ψ)).IsRightAdjoint :=
163	  Functor.isRightAdjoint_of_iso (pushforwardComp.{v} φ ψ)
164	
165	/-- The composition of two pullback functors on sheaves of modules identifies
166	to the pullback for the composition. -/
167	noncomputable def pullbackComp :
168	    pullback.{v} φ ⋙ pullback.{v} ψ ≅
169	      pullback.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).map ψ) :=
170	  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso
171	    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} φ) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} ψ)
172	    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} (F := F ⋙ G)
173	      (φ ≫ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).map ψ))
174	    (pushforwardComp φ ψ)
175	
176	@[simp]
177	lemma conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_inv :
178	    conjugateEquiv ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} φ).comp
179	      (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} ψ))
180	    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} _) (pullbackComp.{v} φ ψ).inv =
181	    (pushforwardComp.{v} φ ψ).hom :=
182	  Adjunction.conjugateEquiv_leftAdjointCompIso_inv _ _ _ _
183	
184	variable {G' : D' ⥤ D''} {R'' : Sheaf K'' RingCat.{u}}
185	  [Functor.IsContinuous G' K' K'']
186	  [Functor.IsContinuous (G ⋙ G') K K'']
187	  [Functor.IsContinuous ((F ⋙ G) ⋙ G') J K'']
188	  [Functor.IsContinuous (F ⋙ G ⋙ G') J K'']
189	  (ψ' : R' ⟶ (G'.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} K' K'').obj R'')
190	
191	variable [(pushforward.{v} ψ').IsRightAdjoint]
192	
193	lemma pullback_assoc :
194	    isoWhiskerLeft _ (pullbackComp.{v} ψ ψ') ≪≫
195	      pullbackComp.{v} (G := G ⋙ G') φ
196	        (ψ ≫ (G.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} K K').map ψ') =
197	    (associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫ isoWhiskerRight (pullbackComp.{v} φ ψ) _ ≪≫
198	      pullbackComp.{v} (F := F ⋙ G)
199	        (φ ≫ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).map ψ) ψ' :=
200	  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_assoc _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (pushforward_assoc φ ψ ψ')
201	
202	end
203	
204	lemma pullback_id_comp :
205	    pullbackComp.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S) φ =
206	      isoWhiskerRight (pullbackId S) (pullback φ) ≪≫ Functor.leftUnitor _ :=
207	  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_id_comp _ _ _ _ (pushforward_comp_id φ)
208	
209	lemma pullback_comp_id :
210	    pullbackComp.{v} (G := 𝟭 _) φ (𝟙 R) =
211	      isoWhiskerLeft _ (pullbackId R) ≪≫ Functor.rightUnitor _ :=
212	  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_comp_id _ _ _ _ (pushforward_id_comp φ)

1	/-

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Tilde
7	import Mathlib.RingTheory.LocalProperties.Exactness
8	import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.LeftExact
9	
10	/-!
11	# Exactness of the tilde functor (Stacks 01HV) — Route-P step P3
12	
13	Project-local supplement feeding `AlgebraicGeometry.qcoh_kernel_qcoh`.
14	
15	For `X = Spec R`, the tilde functor `~ : ModuleCat R ⥤ (Spec R).Modules`,
16	`M ↦ M^~`, is exact.  The named target of this file is
17	`AlgebraicGeometry.tildePreservesFiniteLimits : PreservesFiniteLimits (tilde.functor R)`
18	(the *left*-exactness / kernel-preservation half).
19	
20	## What is delivered (axiom-clean)
21	
22	* `tilde_preservesFiniteColimits` — the *right*-exactness half: `~` is a left adjoint
23	  (`AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.adjunction`), hence preserves all colimits, in particular finite
24	  colimits.  This is one of the two halves of exactness.
25	* `tilde_toStalk_map_injective` — the *flatness core* in the only publicly-accessible form:
26	  for an injective `R`-module map `f : M ⟶ N`, the localised stalk map
27	  `M_𝔭 →ₗ[R] N_𝔭` (built from Mathlib's `IsLocalizedModule (tilde.toStalk · x)` instances) is
28	  injective.  This is the algebraic content that "localisation `R → R_𝔭` is flat" contributes
29	  to mono-preservation.
30	
31	## What is delivered (axiom-clean), continued
32	
33	* `tilde_stalkFunctor_map_toStalk` — the **germ-naturality** transport identity (the crux flagged
34	  by the planner).  For `f : M ⟶ N` and a point `x ↔ 𝔭`, the `Ab`-valued stalk map of `~f`
35	  (computed through the faithful, limit-preserving `Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf`) intertwines the two
36	  localisation maps `tilde.toStalk`: `toStalk M x ≫ (Ab-stalk map) = f ≫ toStalk N x`.  This
37	  identifies the otherwise opaque `Ab`-germ-induced stalk map with the localised module map of `f`
38	  on the image of `toStalk`.  Proven on the public `Ab`-stalk path (`stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply` +
39	  the `⊤`-section naturality `StructureSheaf.comapₗ_const`), avoiding the module-private handles.
40	* `tildePreservesFiniteLimits_of_toPresheaf` — the **categorical reduction**: since
41	  `Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf` reflects finite limits (faithful + preserves limits + reflects isos,
42	  and `(Spec R).Modules` has finite limits), `~` preserves finite limits as soon as the composite
43	  `~ ⋙ toPresheaf` does.  This is `Limits.preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves`.
44	
45	## Why `tildePreservesFiniteLimits` itself is NOT closed here
46	
47	The mathematical route (blueprint `lem:tilde_preserves_kernels`) is stalkwise flatness.  The
48	**categorical-glue obstruction is FALSE** — `tildePreservesFiniteLimits_of_toPresheaf` (above)
49	discharges it via `preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves`; no "right-exact + mono ⟹
50	left-exact" lemma is needed.  The single remaining gap is the **stalkwise localisation step**:
51	showing the composite `~ ⋙ Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf` preserves finite limits.  Stalkwise this is
52	exactly localisation-is-flat:
53	* The `Ab`-germ-induced stalk map of `~f` is identified on the image of `toStalk` with the localised
54	  map of `f` by `tilde_stalkFunctor_map_toStalk`; and the localised map is injective
55	  (`tilde_toStalk_map_injective`).
56	* What still has to be built (~100–150 LOC): upgrade this to a full stalkwise *isomorphism* of the
57	  kernel-comparison map.  Concretely, (a) prove the `Ab` stalk map is `R`-linear (via `germₗ` +
58	  `R`-linearity of `Scheme.Modules.Hom.app`) so it equals `IsLocalizedModule.map …`, then (b)
59	  feed `∀ x, PreservesFiniteLimits (~ ⋙ toPresheaf ⋙ stalkFunctor x)` through a jointly-reflecting
60	  stalk family (`CategoryTheory.JointlyReflectIsomorphisms.jointlyReflectsLimit`) to obtain
61	  `PreservesFiniteLimits (~ ⋙ toPresheaf)`, then `tildePreservesFiniteLimits_of_toPresheaf`.
62	  The `ModuleCat R`-valued stalk path is dead (Mathlib privacy of `toStalkₗ'`, `stalkIsoₗ`,
63	  `stalkToLocalizationₗ`, `structurePresheafInModuleCat`); use the public `Ab` path throughout.
64	
65	See `task_results/AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.TildeExactness.md` for the precise next steps.
66	-/
67	
68	universe u
69	
70	open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry
71	
72	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
73	
74	variable {R : CommRingCat.{u}}
75	
76	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — exactness of the tilde functor -/
77	
78	/-- **Right-exactness of `~`.**  The tilde functor `~ : ModuleCat R ⥤ (Spec R).Modules`
79	preserves finite colimits: it is a left adjoint (`AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.adjunction`), so it
80	preserves all colimits.  Project-local because the packaged statement is what the
81	kernel/cokernel quasi-coherence argument (Stacks `lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent`)
82	consumes alongside the (still open) finite-limit half. -/
83	theorem tilde_preservesFiniteColimits :
84	    Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits (tilde.functor R) := inferInstance
85	
86	/-- **Flatness core of mono-preservation for `~`.**  For an injective `R`-module map
87	`f : M ⟶ N` and a point `x ↔ 𝔭` of `Spec R`, the induced localised map on stalks
88	`M_𝔭 →ₗ[R] N_𝔭` — assembled from Mathlib's `IsLocalizedModule (tilde.toStalk · x).hom`
89	instances via `IsLocalizedModule.map` — is injective.  This is exactly the contribution of
90	"localisation `R → R_𝔭` is flat" to the statement that `~` preserves monomorphisms (Stacks
91	01HV, exactness of `~`).  Stated with the publicly-accessible stalk-localisation map
92	`AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.toStalk`, the only such handle exported by Mathlib. -/
93	theorem tilde_toStalk_map_injective {M N : ModuleCat R} (f : M ⟶ N)
94	    (hf : Function.Injective f.hom) (x : PrimeSpectrum.Top R) :
95	    Function.Injective (IsLocalizedModule.map x.asIdeal.primeCompl
96	      (AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.toStalk M x).hom (AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.toStalk N x).hom f.hom) :=
97	  IsLocalizedModule.map_injective _ _ _ _ hf
98	
99	/-- **Reduction of the named target.**  `tildePreservesFiniteLimits` follows once `~` is shown to
100	preserve every kernel `parallelPair f 0`; all the ambient typeclass hypotheses of
101	`Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels` are already discharged for
102	`tilde.functor R` (it is additive, `ModuleCat R` and `(Spec R).Modules` have the requisite
103	finite (co)products / zero objects).  Recorded project-locally so the remaining obligation is a
104	single, sharply-stated hypothesis for the continuation lane. -/
105	theorem tilde_preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels
106	    (H : ∀ {M N : ModuleCat R} (f : M ⟶ N),
107	      PreservesLimit (parallelPair f 0) (tilde.functor R)) :
108	    PreservesFiniteLimits (tilde.functor R) :=
109	  Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels _
110	
111	/-- **Germ-naturality of the localisation map `toStalk`.**  For an `R`-module map
112	`f : M ⟶ N` and a point `x ↔ 𝔭` of `Spec R`, the `Ab`-valued stalk map of `~f` (computed via the
113	faithful, limit-preserving forgetful functor `Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf`) intertwines the two
114	localisation maps `tilde.toStalk`: precomposing with `toStalk M x` and postcomposing `f` agree.
115	
116	This is the load-bearing transport identity for mono/kernel preservation of `~`: it identifies the
117	otherwise opaque `Ab`-germ-induced stalk map with the localised module map of `f`.  Project-local
118	because Mathlib only exports the localisation handles `tilde.toStalk` and `toOpenₗ` and the section
119	naturality `comapₗ_const`; the germ-level statement is assembled here. -/
120	theorem tilde_stalkFunctor_map_toStalk {M N : ModuleCat R} (f : M ⟶ N)
121	    (x : PrimeSpectrum.Top R) (m : M) :
122	    (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor _ x).map
123	        ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf (Spec (.of R))).map (tilde.map f))
124	        ((tilde.toStalk M x).hom m)
125	      = (tilde.toStalk N x).hom (f.hom m) := by
126	  change (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor _ x).map
127	        ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf (Spec (.of R))).map (tilde.map f))
128	        (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (AlgebraicGeometry.moduleStructurePresheaf R M).presheaf ⊤ x
129	          (by trivial) (StructureSheaf.toOpenₗ R M ⊤ m))
130	      = TopCat.Presheaf.germ (AlgebraicGeometry.moduleStructurePresheaf R N).presheaf ⊤ x
131	          (by trivial) (StructureSheaf.toOpenₗ R N ⊤ (f.hom m))
132	  erw [TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply ⊤ x True.intro
133	    ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf (Spec (.of R))).map (tilde.map f)) (StructureSheaf.toOpenₗ R M ⊤ m)]
134	  congr 1
135	  simp only [Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf_map, Scheme.Modules.mapPresheaf_app,
136	    Scheme.Modules.Hom.app]
137	  rw [StructureSheaf.toOpenₗ_eq_const, StructureSheaf.toOpenₗ_eq_const]
138	  simp only [AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.map, AlgebraicGeometry.SpecModulesToSheafFullyFaithful,
139	    CategoryTheory.NatTrans.comp_app, AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.modulesSpecToSheafIso,
140	    ModuleCat.hom_comp]
141	  erw [StructureSheaf.comapₗ_const (hb := le_of_eq PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen_one.symm)]
142	  rfl
143	
144	/-- **Reduction of `tildePreservesFiniteLimits` to the presheaf level.**  The forgetful functor
145	`Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf` from `𝒪_{Spec R}`-modules to presheaves of abelian groups is faithful,
146	preserves limits, and reflects isomorphisms; hence (since `(Spec R).Modules` has finite limits) it
147	reflects finite limits.  Therefore, to show `~` preserves finite limits it suffices to show the
148	composite `~ ⋙ toPresheaf` does.  This isolates the remaining obligation of
149	`lem:tilde_preserves_kernels` to a statement about the abelian-presheaf-valued composite, whose
150	stalks are computed by `tilde_stalkFunctor_map_toStalk`.  Project-local categorical glue (it refutes
151	the earlier-feared "no right-exact + mono ⟹ left-exact" obstruction: the reduction is purely
152	`preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves`). -/
153	theorem tildePreservesFiniteLimits_of_toPresheaf
154	    (H : PreservesFiniteLimits
155	      (tilde.functor R ⋙ Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf (Spec (.of R)))) :
156	    PreservesFiniteLimits (tilde.functor R) :=
157	  haveI := H
158	  Limits.preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves (tilde.functor R)
159	    (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf (Spec (.of R)))
160	
161	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — R-linear packaging of the Ab-stalk map -/
162	
163	/-- **Germ–scalar compatibility (`R`-linearity of the germ map).**  For `s` a section of `M^~`
164	over `U` and `r : R`, the germ at `x` of `(algebraMap R Γ(O_X,U) r) • s` equals `r •` the germ of
165	`s` (the `R`-action on the stalk being the localisation one through `tilde.toStalk R x`).  This is
166	the section-level half of "the `Ab`-stalk map of `~f` is `R`-linear".  Project-local because the
167	linear germ `StructureSheaf.germₗ` is not exported (no `public`); it is rebuilt here from the public
168	`PresheafOfModules.germ_smul` and `StructureSheaf.algebraMap_germ_apply`. -/
169	theorem tilde_germ_algebraMap_smul {M : ModuleCat R} (U : (Spec (.of R)).Opens)
170	    (x : PrimeSpectrum.Top R) (hxU : x ∈ U) (r : R) (s : Γ(AlgebraicGeometry.tilde M, U)) :
171	    (ConcreteCategory.hom
172	        ((AlgebraicGeometry.tilde M).presheaf.germ U x hxU))
173	        ((algebraMap R Γ(Spec (.of R), U) r) • s)
174	      = r • (ConcreteCategory.hom
175	        ((AlgebraicGeometry.tilde M).presheaf.germ U x hxU)) s := by
176	  erw [PresheafOfModules.germ_smul, StructureSheaf.algebraMap_germ_apply]
177	  rfl
178	
179	/-- **Sub-step (A): the `Ab`-stalk map `σ_x` is `R`-linear.**  The stalk-functor image
180	`σ_x := (stalkFunctor Ab x).map (toPresheaf.map (~f))` is a priori only an `Ab`-morphism between
181	the stalks; this packages it as the genuine `R`-linear map `M_𝔭 →ₗ[R] N_𝔭`.  Project-local: the
182	`ModuleCat R`-valued stalk functor for `SheafOfModules` is not exported (its building blocks
183	`stalkIsoₗ`/`toStalkₗ'` are private), so the linear structure is reconstructed here on the public
184	`Ab` stalk via germ-linearity. -/
185	noncomputable def stalkMapₗ {M N : ModuleCat R} (f : M ⟶ N) (x : PrimeSpectrum.Top R) :

/-!
# Pushforward of presheaves of modules

If `F : C ⥤ D`, the precomposition `F.op ⋙ _` induces a functor from presheaves
over `D` to presheaves over `C`. When `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat`, we define the
induced functor `pushforward₀ : PresheafOfModules.{v} R ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} (F.op ⋙ R)`
on presheaves of modules.

In case we have a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, we also construct
a functor `pushforward : PresheafOfModules.{v} R ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} S`, and
we show that they interact with the composition of morphisms similarly as pseudofunctors.

-/

@[expose] public section

/-- Implementation of `pushforward₀`. -/
@[simps]
def pushforward₀Obj (R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}) (M : PresheafOfModules R) :
    PresheafOfModules (F.op ⋙ R) :=
  { obj X := ModuleCat.of _ (M.obj (F.op.obj X))
    map {X Y} f := M.map (F.op.map f)
    map_id X := by
      refine ModuleCat.hom_ext
        -- Work around an instance diamond for `restrictScalarsId'`
        (@LinearMap.ext _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (_) (_) _ _ _ (fun x => ?_))
      exact (M.congr_map_apply (F.op.map_id X) x).trans (by simp)
    map_comp := fun f g ↦ by
      refine ModuleCat.hom_ext
        -- Work around an instance diamond for `restrictScalarsId'`
        (@LinearMap.ext _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (_) (_) _ _ _ (fun x => ?_))
      exact (M.congr_map_apply (F.op.map_comp f g) x).trans (by simp) }

/-- The pushforward functor on presheaves of modules for a functor `F : C ⥤ D` and
`R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat`. On the underlying presheaves of abelian groups, it is induced
by the precomposition with `F.op`. -/
def pushforward₀ (R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}) :
    PresheafOfModules.{v} R ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} (F.op ⋙ R) where
  obj M := pushforward₀Obj F R M
  map {M₁ M₂} φ := { app X := φ.app _ }

/-- If `F : C ⥤ D` if a functor and `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat` is a presheaf
of commutative rings, this is the pushforward functor from the category
of presheaves of modules on `R` to the category of presheaves of
modules on `F.op ⋙ R`. -/
abbrev pushforward₀OfCommRingCat (R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) :
    PresheafOfModules.{v} (R ⋙ forget₂ _ _) ⥤
      PresheafOfModules.{v} ((F.op ⋙ R) ⋙ forget₂ _ _) :=
  pushforward₀ F (R ⋙ forget₂ _ _)

/-- The pushforward of presheaves of modules commutes with the forgetful functor
to presheaves of abelian groups. -/
noncomputable def pushforward₀CompToPresheaf (R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}) :
    pushforward₀.{v} F R ⋙ toPresheaf _ ≅ toPresheaf _ ⋙ (whiskeringLeft _ _ _).obj F.op :=
  Iso.refl _

14	
15	Let `S` and `R` be sheaves of rings over sites `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` respectively.
16	Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor between these sites, and
17	let `φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R` be a morphism

21	`pullback.{v} φ : SheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} R`
22	that is left adjoint to `pushforward.{v} φ`. We show that it exists
23	under suitable assumptions, and prove that the pullback of (pre)sheaves of
24	modules commutes with the sheafification.
25

27	similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.

import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf
import Mathlib.Topology.Sheaves.Stalks
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Cover.Open

/-!
## Project-local Mathlib supplement — cover-localization iso criterion for `Scheme.Modules`

A morphism `φ : M ⟶ N` of sheaves of modules on a scheme `X` is an isomorphism iff its
restriction to each member of an open cover `𝒰` is an isomorphism.  Mathlib has the
"iso ⟺ iso on every open" criterion (`Scheme.Modules.Hom.isIso_iff_isIso_app`) and the
"restrict-to-open-immersion vs. stalk" comparison (`Scheme.Modules.restrictStalkNatIso`), but not
this *joint* cover-conservativity statement.  It is the keystone of the open-immersion
Beck–Chevalley leaf of the flat-base-change development (Stacks 02KH): it lets one verify that the
base-change comparison morphism is an isomorphism by checking it on the members of an affine cover.

The reverse (content) direction goes through the underlying presheaves of abelian groups: the
forgetful functor `Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X` reflects isomorphisms, presheaves of modules are
sheaves of abelian groups (`Scheme.Modules.isSheaf`), and isomorphy of a sheaf-of-`Ab` morphism is
detected on stalks (`TopCat.Presheaf.isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso`); the per-point reduction to a
cover member is exactly `Scheme.Modules.restrictStalkNatIso`.
-/

open AlgebraicGeometry CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Hom

/-- A morphism of sheaves of modules on a scheme is an isomorphism iff its restriction to every
member of an open cover is an isomorphism.  This is the joint cover-conservativity of the family of
restriction functors `{restrictFunctor (𝒰.f j)}`; project-local because Mathlib only packages the
single-open criterion `isIso_iff_isIso_app` and the per-leg stalk comparison `restrictStalkNatIso`,
not this assembled cover statement. -/
theorem isIso_iff_isIso_restrict
    {X : Scheme} {M N : X.Modules} (φ : M ⟶ N) (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) :
    IsIso φ ↔ ∀ j, IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (𝒰.f j)).map φ) := by
  constructor
  · -- (⟹) restriction functors preserve isomorphisms.
    intro h j
    haveI := h
    infer_instance
  · -- (⟸) the content direction.
    intro hj
    -- It suffices that the underlying presheaf morphism is an iso: `toPresheaf X` reflects isos.
    haveI key : IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ) := by
      -- Present `M`, `N` as sheaves of abelian groups and `φ` as a morphism of `TopCat.Sheaf Ab`.
      set F : TopCat.Sheaf Ab X.carrier := ⟨M.presheaf, M.isSheaf⟩ with hF
      set G : TopCat.Sheaf Ab X.carrier := ⟨N.presheaf, N.isSheaf⟩ with hG
      set fS : F ⟶ G := ⟨(Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ⟩ with hfS_def
      -- It suffices that `fS` be an iso: `Sheaf.forget` sends it to `(toPresheaf X).map φ`.
      suffices hfS : IsIso fS by
        haveI : IsIso fS := hfS
        exact Functor.map_isIso (TopCat.Sheaf.forget Ab X.carrier) fS
      -- Detect isomorphy of the sheaf-of-`Ab` morphism on stalks.
      rw [TopCat.Presheaf.isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso]
      intro x
      change IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab x).map ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ))
      -- Choose a cover member through `x` and a preimage point `y`.
      set j := 𝒰.idx x with hj_def
      obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := 𝒰.covers x
      rw [← hy]
      -- The restricted morphism is an iso (hyp); push it through the functors to its `y`-stalk.
      haveI hrestr := hj j
      have hstalk : IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab y).map
          ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf (𝒰.X j)).map
            ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (𝒰.f j)).map φ))) :=
        Functor.map_isIso _ _
      -- `restrictStalkNatIso` conjugates the `y`-stalk of the restriction with `φ`'s `x`-stalk.
      exact (NatIso.isIso_map_iff (Scheme.Modules.restrictStalkNatIso (𝒰.f j) y) φ).mp hstalk
    exact isIso_of_reflects_iso φ (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X)

end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Hom

/-!

# Module structure on stalks
Let `M` be a presheaf of `R`-modules on a topological space. We endow `M.presheaf.stalk x` with
an `R.stalk x`-module structure.

The key characterizing lemma is `PresheafOfModules.germ_smul`, which describes the compatibility
of the scalar action and `TopCat.Presheaf.germ`.

-/

@[expose] public section

open CategoryTheory LinearMap Opposite TopologicalSpace

universe w₀ w u v

namespace CategoryTheory.Limits

open IsFiltered

variable {C : Type*} [SmallCategory C] [IsFiltered C] (R : C ⥤ RingCat) (M : C ⥤ Ab)
    [∀ i, Module (R.obj i) (M.obj i)]
    (H : ∀ {i j} (f : i ⟶ j) r m, M.map f (r • m) = R.map f r • M.map f m)

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- (Implementation). The scalar multiplication function on `ColimitType`. -/
protected noncomputable
def colimit.smul (r : (R ⋙ forget _).ColimitType) (m : (M ⋙ forget _).ColimitType) :
    (M ⋙ forget _).ColimitType := by
  refine Quot.liftOn₂ r m (fun Ua Vb ↦ Functor.ιColimitType _ (max Ua.1 Vb.1) <|
    letI a : R.obj (max Ua.1 Vb.1) := R.map (leftToMax Ua.1 Vb.1) Ua.2
    letI b : M.obj (max Ua.1 Vb.1) := M.map (rightToMax Ua.1 Vb.1) Vb.2
    a • b) ?_ ?_
  · rintro ⟨U, a⟩ ⟨V₁, b₁⟩ ⟨V₂, b₂⟩ ⟨f : V₁ ⟶ V₂, rfl : b₂ = M.map _ b₁⟩
    obtain ⟨s, α, β, h₁, h₂⟩ :=
      bowtie (leftToMax U V₁) (leftToMax U V₂)
        (rightToMax U V₁) (f ≫ rightToMax U V₂)
    refine Functor.ιColimitType_eq_of_map_eq_map _ _ _ α β ?_
    simp [*, ← R.map_comp_apply, ← M.map_comp_apply, -Functor.map_comp]
  · rintro ⟨U₁, a₁⟩ ⟨U₂, a₂⟩ ⟨V, b⟩ ⟨f : U₁ ⟶ U₂, rfl : a₂ = R.map _ a₁⟩
    obtain ⟨s, α, β, h₁, h₂⟩ :=
      bowtie (leftToMax U₁ V) (f ≫ leftToMax U₂ V)
        (rightToMax U₁ V) (rightToMax U₂ V)
    refine Functor.ιColimitType_eq_of_map_eq_map _ _ _ α β ?_
    simp [*, ← R.map_comp_apply, ← M.map_comp_apply, -Functor.map_comp]

#adaptation_note /-- As of nightly-2026-02-10, we need to increase the maxHeartbeats limits here. -/
set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 40000 in --
/-- (Implementation). The module structure on `AddCommGrpCat.FilteredColimits.colimit`. -/
noncomputable abbrev filteredColimitsModule : Module (RingCat.FilteredColimits.colimit R)
    (AddCommGrpCat.FilteredColimits.colimit M) where
  smul := colimit.smul R M H
  mul_smul r s m := Quot.induction_on₃ r s m <| by
    rintro ⟨U₁, a₁⟩ ⟨U₂, a₂⟩ ⟨V, b⟩
    obtain ⟨s, α, β, h₁, h₂, h₃⟩ := crown₃
      (leftToMax U₁ U₂ ≫ leftToMax (max U₁ U₂) V) (leftToMax U₁ (max U₂ V))
      (rightToMax U₁ U₂ ≫ leftToMax (max U₁ U₂) V) (leftToMax U₂ V ≫ rightToMax U₁ (max U₂ V))
      (rightToMax (max U₁ U₂) V) (rightToMax U₂ V ≫ rightToMax U₁ (max U₂ V))
    refine Functor.ιColimitType_eq_of_map_eq_map _ _ _ α β ?_
    dsimp
    simp only [map_mul, ← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, mul_smul, *]
  one_smul m := Quot.induction_on m <| by
    rintro ⟨V, b⟩
    refine Functor.ιColimitType_eq_of_map_eq_map _ _ _ (𝟙 _) (rightToMax _ _) ?_

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2024 Joël Riou. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: Joël Riou
5	-/
6	module
7	
8	public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Presheaf.Generator
9	public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Presheaf.Pushforward
10	public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.PartialAdjoint
11	public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.CompositionIso
12	
13	/-!
14	# Pullback of presheaves of modules
15	
16	Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a functor, `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` and `S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` be presheaves
17	of rings, and `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R` be a morphism of presheaves of rings,
18	we introduce the pullback functor `pullback : PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R`
19	as the left adjoint of `pushforward : PresheafOfModules R ⥤ PresheafOfModules S`.
20	The existence of this left adjoint functor is obtained under suitable universe assumptions.
21	
22	From the compatibility of `pushforward` with respect to composition, we deduce
23	similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.
24	
25	-/
26	
27	@[expose] public section
28	
29	universe v v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄ u₁ u₂ u₃ u₄ u
30	
31	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite Functor
32	
33	namespace PresheafOfModules
34	
35	section
36	
37	variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
38	  {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
39	  [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
40	
41	/-- The pullback functor `PresheafOfModules S ⥤ PresheafOfModules R` induced by
42	a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, defined as the left adjoint
43	functor to the pushforward, when it exists. -/
44	noncomputable def pullback : PresheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R :=
45	  (pushforward.{v} φ).leftAdjoint
46	
47	/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, this is the adjunction
48	between associated pullback and pushforward functors on the categories
49	of presheaves of modules. -/
50	noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction : pullback.{v} φ ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
51	  Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (pushforward φ)
52	
53	/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, this is the property
54	that the (partial) left adjoint functor of `pushforward φ` is defined
55	on a certain object `M : PresheafOfModules S`. -/
56	abbrev pullbackObjIsDefined : ObjectProperty (PresheafOfModules.{v} S) :=
57	  (pushforward φ).leftAdjointObjIsDefined
58	
59	end
60	
61	section
62	
63	variable {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
64	  {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
65	
66	/-- Given a morphism of presheaves of rings `φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R`, where `F : C ⥤ D`,
67	`S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat`, `R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` and `X : C`, the (partial) left adjoint
68	functor of `pushforward φ` is defined on the object `(free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)`:
69	this object shall be mapped to `(free R).obj (yoneda.obj (F.obj X))`. -/
70	noncomputable def pushforwardCompCoyonedaFreeYonedaCorepresentableBy (X : C) :
71	    (pushforward φ ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op ((free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)))).CorepresentableBy
72	      ((free R).obj (yoneda.obj (F.obj X))) where
73	  homEquiv {M} := freeYonedaEquiv.trans
74	    (freeYonedaEquiv (M := (pushforward φ).obj M)).symm
75	  homEquiv_comp {M N} g f := freeYonedaEquiv.injective (by
76	    dsimp
77	    erw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply, freeYonedaEquiv_comp]
78	    conv_rhs => erw [freeYonedaEquiv_comp]
79	    erw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
80	    rfl)
81	
82	lemma pullbackObjIsDefined_free_yoneda (X : C) :
83	    pullbackObjIsDefined φ ((free S).obj (yoneda.obj X)) :=
84	  (pushforwardCompCoyonedaFreeYonedaCorepresentableBy φ X).isCorepresentable
85	
86	lemma pullbackObjIsDefined_eq_top :
87	    pullbackObjIsDefined.{u} φ = ⊤ := by
88	  ext M
89	  simp only [Pi.top_apply, Prop.top_eq_true, iff_true]
90	  apply leftAdjointObjIsDefined_of_isColimit
91	    M.isColimitFreeYonedaCoproductsCokernelCofork
92	  rintro (_ | _)
93	  all_goals
94	    apply leftAdjointObjIsDefined_colimit _
95	      (fun _ ↦ pullbackObjIsDefined_free_yoneda _ _)
96	
97	instance : (pushforward.{u} φ).IsRightAdjoint :=
98	  isRightAdjoint_of_leftAdjointObjIsDefined_eq_top
99	    (pullbackObjIsDefined_eq_top φ)
100	
101	end
102	
103	section
104	
105	variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
106	  {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} E] {E' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} E']
107	
108	variable {F : C ⥤ D} {R : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {S : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (φ : S ⟶ F.op ⋙ R)
109	  {G : D ⥤ E} {T : Eᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} (ψ : R ⟶ G.op ⋙ T)
110	
111	instance : (pushforward.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S)).IsRightAdjoint :=
112	  isRightAdjoint_of_iso (pushforwardId.{v} S).symm
113	
114	variable (S) in
115	/-- The pullback by the identity morphism identifies to the identity functor of the
116	category of presheaves of modules. -/
117	noncomputable def pullbackId : pullback.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S) ≅ 𝟭 _ :=
118	  ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S))).leftAdjointIdIso (pushforwardId S)
119	
120	variable [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
121	
122	section
123	
124	variable [(pushforward.{v} ψ).IsRightAdjoint]
125	
126	instance : (pushforward.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ)).IsRightAdjoint :=
127	  isRightAdjoint_of_iso (pushforwardComp.{v} φ ψ)
128	
129	/-- The composition of two pullback functors on presheaves of modules identifies
130	to the pullback for the composition. -/
131	noncomputable def pullbackComp :
132	    pullback.{v} φ ⋙ pullback.{v} ψ ≅
133	      pullback.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ) :=
134	  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso
135	    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} φ) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} ψ)
136	    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ whiskerLeft F.op ψ))
137	    (pushforwardComp φ ψ)
138	
139	variable {T' : E'ᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}} {G' : E ⥤ E'} (ψ' : T ⟶ G'.op ⋙ T')
140	  [(pushforward.{v} ψ').IsRightAdjoint]

6	module
7	
8	public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Presheaf.Pullback
9	public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Presheaf.Sheafification
10	public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.PushforwardContinuous
11	
12	/-!
13	# Pullback of sheaves of modules
14	
15	Let `S` and `R` be sheaves of rings over sites `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` respectively.
16	Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor between these sites, and
17	let `φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R` be a morphism
18	of sheaves of rings.
19	
20	In this file, we define the pullback functor for sheaves of modules
21	`pullback.{v} φ : SheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} R`
22	that is left adjoint to `pushforward.{v} φ`. We show that it exists
23	under suitable assumptions, and prove that the pullback of (pre)sheaves of
24	modules commutes with the sheafification.
25	
26	From the compatibility of `pushforward` with respect to composition, we deduce
27	similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.
28	
29	-/
30	
31	@[expose] public section
32	
33	universe v v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄ u₁ u₂ u₃ u₄ u
34	
35	open CategoryTheory Functor
36	
37	namespace SheafOfModules
38	
39	variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
40	  {D' : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} D'] {D'' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} D'']
41	  {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} {F : C ⥤ D}
42	  {S : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} {R : Sheaf K RingCat.{u}}
43	  [Functor.IsContinuous F J K]
44	  (φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R)
45	
46	section
47	
48	variable [(pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint]
49	
50	/-- The pullback functor `SheafOfModules S ⥤ SheafOfModules R` induced by
51	a morphism of sheaves of rings `S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R`,
52	defined as the left adjoint functor to the pushforward, when it exists. -/
53	noncomputable def pullback : SheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} R :=
54	  (pushforward.{v} φ).leftAdjoint
55	
56	/-- Given a continuous functor between sites `F`, and a morphism of sheaves of rings
57	`S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R`, this is the adjunction
58	between the corresponding pullback and pushforward functors on the categories
59	of sheaves of modules. -/
60	noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction : pullback.{v} φ ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
61	  Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (pushforward φ)
62	
63	instance : (pullback.{v} φ).IsLeftAdjoint :=
64	  (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ).isLeftAdjoint
65	
66	end
67	
68	section
69	
70	variable [(PresheafOfModules.pushforward.{v} φ.hom).IsRightAdjoint]
71	  [HasWeakSheafify K AddCommGrpCat.{v}] [K.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
72	
73	namespace PullbackConstruction
74	
75	set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
76	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
77	/-- Construction of a left adjoint to the functor `pushforward.{v} φ` by using the
78	pullback of presheaves of modules and the sheafification. -/
79	noncomputable def adjunction :
80	    (forget S ⋙ PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ.hom ⋙
81	      PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj)) ⊣ pushforward.{v} φ :=
82	  Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv
83	    { homEquiv := fun F G ↦
84	        ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 R.obj)).homEquiv _ _).trans
85	            (((PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ.hom).homEquiv F.val G.val).trans
86	              ((fullyFaithfulForget S).homEquiv (Y := (pushforward φ).obj G)).symm)
87	      homEquiv_naturality_left_symm := by
88	        intros
89	        dsimp [Functor.FullyFaithful.homEquiv]
90	        -- these erw seem difficult to remove
91	        erw [Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm,
92	          Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm]
93	        dsimp [pushforward_obj_val]
94	        simp only [Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc]
95	      homEquiv_naturality_right := by
96	        tauto }
97	
98	end PullbackConstruction
99	
100	instance : (pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint :=
101	  (PullbackConstruction.adjunction.{v} φ).isRightAdjoint
102	
103	/-- The pullback functor on sheaves of modules can be described as a composition
104	of the forget functor to presheaves, the pullback on presheaves of modules, and
105	the sheafification functor. -/
106	noncomputable def pullbackIso :
107	    pullback.{v} φ ≅
108	      forget S ⋙ PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ.hom ⋙
109	        PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj) :=
110	  Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ)
111	    (PullbackConstruction.adjunction φ)
112	
113	section
114	
115	variable [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{v}] [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
116	
117	/-- The pullback of (pre)sheaves of modules commutes with the sheafification. -/
118	noncomputable def sheafificationCompPullback :
119	    PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 S.obj) ⋙ pullback.{v} φ ≅
120	      PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ.hom ⋙
121	        PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj) :=
122	  Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq
123	    ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 S.obj)).comp
124	      (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ))
125	    ((PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ.hom).comp
126	      (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 R.obj)))
127	
128	end
129	
130	end

136	variable (S) in

138	category of sheaves of modules. -/
139	noncomputable def pullbackId : pullback.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S) ≅ 𝟭 _ :=
140	  ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} (F := 𝟭 C) (𝟙 S))).leftAdjointIdIso (pushforwardId S)

148

153	variable {K' : GrothendieckTopology D'} {K'' : GrothendieckTopology D''}
154	  {G : D ⥤ D'} {R' : Sheaf K' RingCat.{u}}

160

162	    (φ ≫ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).map ψ)).IsRightAdjoint :=
163	  Functor.isRightAdjoint_of_iso (pushforwardComp.{v} φ ψ)
164	
165	/-- The composition of two pullback functors on sheaves of modules identifies
166	to the pullback for the composition. -/
167	noncomputable def pullbackComp :
168	    pullback.{v} φ ⋙ pullback.{v} ψ ≅
169	      pullback.{v} (F := F ⋙ G) (φ ≫ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).map ψ) :=
170	  Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso
171	    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} φ) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} ψ)
172	    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} (F := F ⋙ G)
173	      (φ ≫ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).map ψ))
174	    (pushforwardComp φ ψ)
175	
176	@[simp]
177	lemma conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_inv :
178	    conjugateEquiv ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} φ).comp
179	      (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} ψ))
180	    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{v} _) (pullbackComp.{v} φ ψ).inv =
181	    (pushforwardComp.{v} φ ψ).hom :=
182	  Adjunction.conjugateEquiv_leftAdjointCompIso_inv _ _ _ _
183	
184	variable {G' : D' ⥤ D''} {R'' : Sheaf K'' RingCat.{u}}
185	  [Functor.IsContinuous G' K' K'']
186	  [Functor.IsContinuous (G ⋙ G') K K'']
187	  [Functor.IsContinuous ((F ⋙ G) ⋙ G') J K'']
188	  [Functor.IsContinuous (F ⋙ G ⋙ G') J K'']
189	  (ψ' : R' ⟶ (G'.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} K' K'').obj R'')

195	      pullbackComp.{v} (G := G ⋙ G') φ

# Points of a site

Let `C` be a category equipped with a Grothendieck topology `J`. In this file,
we define the notion of point of the site `(C, J)`, as a
structure `GrothendieckTopology.Point`. Such a `Φ : J.Point` consists
in a functor `Φ.fiber : C ⥤ Type w` such that the category `Φ.fiber.Elements`
is cofiltered (and initially small) and such that if `x : Φ.fiber.obj X`
and `R` is a covering sieve of `X`, then `x` belongs to the image
of some `y : Φ.fiber.obj Y` by a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` which belongs to `R`.
(This definition is essentially the definition of a fiber functor on a site
from SGA 4 IV 6.3.)

The fact that `Φ.fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ` is filtered allows to define
`Φ.presheafFiber : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A` by taking the filtering colimit
of the evaluation functors at `op X` when `(X : C, x : F.obj X)` varies in
`Φ.fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ`. We define `Φ.sheafFiber : Sheaf J A ⥤ A` as the
restriction of `Φ.presheafFiber` to the full subcategory of sheaves.

Under certain assumptions, we show that if `A` is concrete and
`P ⟶ Q` is a locally bijective morphism between presheaves,
then the induced morphism on fibers is a bijection. It follows
that not only `Φ.sheafFiber : Sheaf J A ⥤ A` is the restriction of
`Φ.presheafFiber` but it may also be thought as a localization
of this functor with respect to the class of morphisms `J.W`.

--- Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Point/Conservative.lean
# Conservative families of points

Let `J` be a Grothendieck topology on a category `C`.
Let `P : ObjectProperty J.Point` be a family of points. We say that
`P` is a conservative family of points if the corresponding
fiber functors `Sheaf J (Type w) ⥤ Type w` jointly reflect
isomorphisms. Under suitable assumptions on the coefficient
category `A`, this implies that the fiber functors
`Sheaf J A ⥤ A` corresponding to the points in `P`
jointly reflect isomorphisms, epimorphisms and monomorphisms,
and they are also jointly faithful.

We provide a constructor `ObjectProperty.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints.mk'`
which allows to verify that a family of points is conservative
using a condition involving covering sieves (SGA 4 IV 6.5 (a)).

-/

--- Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Point/OfIsCofiltered.lean
# Alternative constructor for points

Let `J` be a Grothendieck topology on a category `C`. We provide a constructor
`Point.ofIsCofiltered` for points for `J` which takes as inputs:
- a functor `p : N ⥤ C` where `N` is cofiltered and initially small
- the assumption that for any covering sieve `R` of `X`,
  any morphism `f : p.obj U ⟶ X`, there exists a morphism `g : Y ⟶ X` in `R`,
  a morphism `q : V ⟶ U` in `N` and a morphism `a : p.obj V ⟶ Y` such
  that `a ≫ g = p.map q ≫ f`.
We show that the fiber of a presheaf for the constructed point identifies
to a colimit indexed by the category `N`.

-/

def stalkPullbackHom (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Y.Presheaf C) (x : X) :
    F.stalk (f x) ⟶ ((pullback C f).obj F).stalk x :=
  (stalkFunctor _ (f x)).map ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction C f).unit.app F) ≫
    stalkPushforward _ _ _ x

--- Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Point/Basic.lean
# Points of a site

Let `C` be a category equipped with a Grothendieck topology `J`. In this file,
we define the notion of point of the site `(C, J)`, as a
structure `GrothendieckTopology.Point`. Such a `Φ : J.Point` consists
in a functor `Φ.fiber : C ⥤ Type w` such that the category `Φ.fiber.Elements`
is cofiltered (and initially small) and such that if `x : Φ.fiber.obj X`
and `R` is a covering sieve of `X`, then `x` belongs to the image
of some `y : Φ.fiber.obj Y` by a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` which belongs to `R`.
(This definition is essentially the definition of a fiber functor on a site
from SGA 4 IV 6.3.)

The fact that `Φ.fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ` is filtered allows to define
`Φ.presheafFiber : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A` by taking the filtering colimit
of the evaluation functors at `op X` when `(X : C, x : F.obj X)` varies in
`Φ.fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ`. We define `Φ.sheafFiber : Sheaf J A ⥤ A` as the
restriction of `Φ.presheafFiber` to the full subcategory of sheaves.

Under certain assumptions, we show that if `A` is concrete and
`P ⟶ Q` is a locally bijective morphism between presheaves,
then the induced morphism on fibers is a bijection. It follows
that not only `Φ.sheafFiber : Sheaf J A ⥤ A` is the restriction of
`Φ.presheafFiber` but it may also be thought as a localization
of this functor with respect to the class of morphisms `J.W`.

--- Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Point/Conservative.lean
# Conservative families of points

Let `J` be a Grothendieck topology on a category `C`.
Let `P : ObjectProperty J.Point` be a family of points. We say that
`P` is a conservative family of points if the corresponding
fiber functors `Sheaf J (Type w) ⥤ Type w` jointly reflect
isomorphisms. Under suitable assumptions on the coefficient
category `A`, this implies that the fiber functors
`Sheaf J A ⥤ A` corresponding to the points in `P`
jointly reflect isomorphisms, epimorphisms and monomorphisms,
and they are also jointly faithful.

We provide a constructor `ObjectProperty.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints.mk'`
which allows to verify that a family of points is conservative
using a condition involving covering sieves (SGA 4 IV 6.5 (a)).

-/

--- Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Point/OfIsCofiltered.lean
# Alternative constructor for points

Let `J` be a Grothendieck topology on a category `C`. We provide a constructor
`Point.ofIsCofiltered` for points for `J` which takes as inputs:
- a functor `p : N ⥤ C` where `N` is cofiltered and initially small
- the assumption that for any covering sieve `R` of `X`,
  any morphism `f : p.obj U ⟶ X`, there exists a morphism `g : Y ⟶ X` in `R`,
  a morphism `q : V ⟶ U` in `N` and a morphism `a : p.obj V ⟶ Y` such
  that `a ≫ g = p.map q ≫ f`.
We show that the fiber of a presheaf for the constructed point identifies
to a colimit indexed by the category `N`.

-/
